items.en: Today, let’s discuss inventions and their roles in shaping our world.
items.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊发明，以及它们在塑造我们世界中的作用。

items.en: Which invention do you think is the most important?
items.zh: 你觉得哪一项发明最重要？

items.en: I believe the invention of paper has greatly influenced the development of human civilization.
items.zh: 我觉得纸的发明对人类文明的发展影响很大。

items.en: How about the telephone?
items.zh: 那电话呢？

items.en: It allows people to communicate with each other easily and quickly.
items.zh: 它让人们能轻松又快速地互相交流。

items.en: The light bulb is also an important invention.
items.zh: 电灯泡也是一项重要的发明。

items.en: It lights up the world.
items.zh: 它照亮了整个世界。

items.en: I think washing machines are helpful inventions, and both electric and gas-powered cars are cool.
items.zh: 我觉得洗衣机是很实用的发明，电动车和燃气车也都很酷。

items.en: These are all very good examples!
items.zh: 这些例子都举得非常好！

items.en: Are there any other inventions coming to your mind?
items.zh: 你们还能想到别的发明吗？

items.en: Computers are very important.
items.zh: 电脑非常重要。

items.en: People can do so much on a computer.
items.zh: 用电脑能做好多事情。

items.en: And don’t forget about the internet!
items.zh: 还有，别忘了互联网！

items.en: It connects people from all over the world and provides us with information, knowledge, and entertainment.
items.zh: 它把世界各地的人连在一起，还给我们带来信息、知识和娱乐。

items.en: Long ago, people did not travel far from home.
items.zh: 很久以前，人们不会离家远行。

items.en: In fact, in the early days, a person might live their whole life in one village and never travel far.
items.zh: 其实在早些年代，一个人可能一辈子都待在一个村子里，从没出过远门。

items.en: The first important invention in travel was the wheel.
items.zh: 出行方面第一项重要发明是轮子。

items.en: And then came the wagons.
items.zh: 接着出现了四轮马车。

items.en: Humans began to have the power to move and carry things across long distances.
items.zh: 人类从此有了长距离搬运和运送东西的能力。

items.en: The next was the train.
items.zh: 接下来是火车。

items.en: After the train came the invention of cars, buses, trucks, and other means of transportation.
items.zh: 火车之后，又有了汽车、公交车、卡车和其他交通工具。

items.en: Humans and goods were able to travel farther than ever before.
items.zh: 人和货物都能走到比以前更远的地方。

items.en: Boats and ships provided another important way of travelling.
items.zh: 小船和大船提供了另一种重要的出行方式。

items.en: The invention of the compass helped people explore more places.
items.zh: 指南针的发明帮助人们探索了更多地方。

items.en: And canal systems made fast waterway transportation possible.
items.zh: 运河系统让快速的水路运输成为可能。

items.en: Modern means of transportation, such as high-speed trains and airplanes, help people travel faster and farther.
items.zh: 高铁、飞机这些现代交通工具，让人们走得更快、更远。

items.en: Eco-friendly electric cars are common and self-driving cars are in development.
items.zh: 环保电动车已经很常见，自动驾驶汽车也在研发中。

items.en: People can even travel to space in spaceships.
items.zh: 人们甚至能坐宇宙飞船去太空。

items.en: Who knows what the future holds?
items.zh: 谁知道未来还会有什么呢？

items.en: The development of transportation has made people’s travel much easier and faster.
items.zh: 交通的发展让人们的出行轻松多了，也快多了。

items.en: Every invention is a symbol of human creativity.
items.zh: 每一项发明都是人类创造力的象征。

items.en: Let’s enjoy these developments and work for more great things in the future.
items.zh: 让我们享受这些成果，也为未来更多了不起的发明努力吧。

items.en: Jenny wants to do her homework on the computer.
items.zh: 珍妮想在电脑上写作业。

items.en: But her mum is using it.
items.zh: 可是妈妈正在用电脑。

items.en: Mum, is it okay if I use the computer now?
items.zh: 妈妈，我现在可以用电脑吗？

items.en: Okay.
items.zh: 可以。

items.en: I just finished my work, so it’s all yours.
items.zh: 我刚忙完工作，电脑归你了。

items.en: Jenny, you’re so lucky to have a computer.
items.zh: 珍妮，你能有台电脑真幸运。

items.en: Yes, I am.
items.zh: 是呀，我很幸运。

items.en: As it’s connected to the internet, it has made study and research much easier.
items.zh: 它连上了互联网，学习和查资料都方便多了。

items.en: This technology helps students a lot with their homework.
items.zh: 这项技术对学生做作业帮助很大。

items.en: But when I was a student, computers were not widely used.
items.zh: 可我上学那会儿，电脑还没普及。

items.en: And the internet was not as convenient as it is now.
items.zh: 互联网也不像现在这么方便。

items.en: I couldn’t imagine having such a convenient tool for getting the job done.
items.zh: 我那时真想象不出能有这么顺手的工具来帮忙完成任务。

items.en: Mum, how was homework done in those days?
items.zh: 妈妈，那时候作业是怎么做的呀？

items.en: Well, everything was written by hand on paper.
items.zh: 嗯，所有东西都得手写在本子上。

items.en: When I didn’t know how to spell a word, I had to look it up in a printed dictionary.
items.zh: 不会拼某个词，就得去翻纸质词典。

items.en: When I needed to do any research, I had to go to the library.
items.zh: 要查资料，就得跑图书馆。

items.en: But now with the internet we can simply search for everything online.
items.zh: 可现在有了互联网，什么都能直接上网搜。

items.en: And there’s always new technology, like AI.
items.zh: 而且还不断有新技术，比如人工智能。

items.en: Yes, and you can easily find definitions and examples for any word.
items.zh: 是啊，任何一个词的释义和例句你都能轻松查到。

items.en: The internet and the computer are amazing inventions with many applications.
items.zh: 互联网和电脑真是了不起的发明，用途特别多。

items.en: I agree with you on that, Mum.
items.zh: 这点我同意您，妈妈。

items.en: While pouring a glass of milk, Jeremy notices something written on the package.
items.zh: 杰瑞米倒牛奶时，注意到包装上写着字。

items.en: Hey, Mum!
items.zh: 嘿，妈妈！

items.en: I just noticed a big word on the carton.
items.zh: 我刚看到盒子上有个大字。

items.en: PASTEURIZED.
items.zh: 「巴氏杀菌」。

items.en: What does it mean?
items.zh: 这是什么意思？

items.en: Well, if something is pasteurized, it means that it has gone through a process of heating to a certain temperature.
items.zh: 嗯，标着「巴氏杀菌」，就是说它经过了一道加热到一定温度的工序。

items.en: Why do we heat milk?
items.zh: 为什么要给牛奶加热呢？

items.en: Raw milk has dangerous bacteria and germs.
items.zh: 生牛奶里有危险的细菌和病菌。

items.en: We must heat milk to 72 degrees Celsius for 15 seconds to kill them.
items.zh: 得把牛奶加热到 72 摄氏度、保持 15 秒，才能杀死它们。

items.en: How did people discover that?
items.zh: 人们是怎么发现这个办法的？

items.en: Many years ago, people sometimes got sick when they drank milk.
items.zh: 很多年前，人们喝牛奶有时会生病。

items.en: Some of them even died because of the bad bacteria.
items.zh: 有些人甚至因为有害细菌丢了性命。

items.en: Wow!
items.zh: 哇！

items.en: Who discovered this heating process?
items.zh: 是谁发现了这种加热方法？

items.en: A dairy farmer or a scientist?
items.zh: 是奶农，还是科学家？

items.en: It was Louis Pasteur, a French microbiologist.
items.zh: 是路易·巴斯德，一位法国微生物学家。

items.en: He discovered the process around 1864.
items.zh: 他在 1864 年前后发现了这个方法。

items.en: That’s a long time ago!
items.zh: 那可真是很久以前了！

items.en: Mr Pasteur was one of the greatest scientists.
items.zh: 巴斯德先生是最伟大的科学家之一。

items.en: His work saved millions of lives around the world.
items.zh: 他的研究救了全世界数以百万计的生命。

items.en: He was famous for his work on germs.
items.zh: 他以研究细菌而闻名。

items.en: Well, here’s a toast to you, Mr Pasteur.
items.zh: 那我敬您一杯，巴斯德先生。

items.en: Thank you for making the world much safer.
items.zh: 谢谢您让这个世界安全多了。

items.en: Ancient times: Ancient China, Greece, and Rome used ice or snow to preserve food by freezing or chilling it.
items.zh: 古代：中国、希腊和罗马用冰或雪冷冻、冷藏食物来保鲜。

items.en: 1600s: Icehouses were used to preserve food all year-round.
items.zh: 17世纪：人们用冰窖全年保存食物。

items.en: 1748: William Cullen did an experiment on artificial refrigeration.
items.zh: 1748年：威廉·卡伦做了一次人工制冷实验。

items.en: 1805: Oliver Evans designed the first refrigeration machine.
items.zh: 1805年：奥利弗·埃文斯设计出第一台制冷机。

items.en: 1890s: Iceboxes became popular.
items.zh: 19世纪90年代：冰盒开始流行。

items.en: They were smaller icehouses meant for home use.
items.zh: 它们是供家庭使用的小型冰窖。

items.en: 1913: Fred W.
items.zh: 1913年：弗雷德·W.

items.en: Wolf invented the first home electric refrigerator.
items.zh: 沃尔夫发明了第一台家用电冰箱。

items.en: 1918: Mass production of home refrigerators began.
items.zh: 1918年：家用电冰箱开始批量生产。

items.en: 1920s: Refrigerators became popular in some countries.
items.zh: 20世纪20年代：电冰箱在一些国家普及开来。

items.en: 1940s: Freezer compartments were added.
items.zh: 20世纪40年代：加装了冷冻室。

items.en: 1980s: Water dispensers were added.
items.zh: 20世纪80年代：加装了饮水机。

items.en: 1996: Refrigerators became more energy-saving.
items.zh: 1996年：电冰箱变得更省电了。

items.en: We all know the most significant inventions of ancient China — paper-making, printing, gunpowder, and compasses.
items.zh: 我们都知道中国古代最重要的发明——造纸术、印刷术、火药和指南针。

items.en: However, Chinese people also made many other fascinating inventions.
items.zh: 不过，中国人还创造了许多别的有趣发明。

items.en: Have you used the abacus?
items.zh: 你用过算盘吗？

items.en: It was invented in China over 2,500 years ago.
items.zh: 它是两千五百多年前在中国发明的。

items.en: It became the primary tool used by merchants and bankers to calculate.
items.zh: 后来成了商人和钱庄老板算账的主要工具。

items.en: Tofu originated in China.
items.zh: 豆腐起源于中国。

items.en: It is a good source of protein.
items.zh: 它是很好的蛋白质来源。

items.en: Tofu is rich in minerals that are important for building strong bones and reducing the risk of some diseases.
items.zh: 豆腐富含矿物质，有助于强健骨骼、降低某些疾病的风险。

items.en: It has been an important part of Chinese cuisine for over 2,000 years and is now enjoyed worldwide.
items.zh: 两千多年来它一直是中国饮食的重要部分，如今全世界都爱吃。

items.en: Tea making is another invention from China.
items.zh: 制茶也是中国的一项发明。

items.en: It is said that Shennong, an ancient Chinese emperor, discovered tea when a tea leaf accidentally fell into a pot of boiling water.
items.zh: 相传中国古代帝王神农，是因为一片茶叶不小心落进滚水里，才发现了茶。

items.en: Today, tea is popular all over the world.
items.zh: 今天，茶已经风靡全球。

items.en: The origins of porcelain can be traced back to the Han Dynasty in China.
items.zh: 瓷器的起源可以追溯到中国的汉代。

items.en: Porcelain quickly spread throughout China and reached other parts of the world.
items.zh: 瓷器很快传遍中国，又走向了世界其他地方。
